claims.text: Exposure above 900 °C in an oxidizing or corrosive environment triggers selective oxidation in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Single-phase CrFeCoNiAl alloys form coherent, adherent protective oxide layers that persist during high-temperature exposure.
Single-phase CrFeCoNiSi alloys form coherent, adherent protective oxide layers that persist during high-temperature exposure.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys promote heterogeneous oxidation and unstable oxide scales prone to cracking and spallation.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys promote heterogeneous oxidation and unstable oxide scales prone to cracking and spallation.
The protective scales on single-phase Al- or Si-containing alloys are continuous and enriched in Al2O3 or SiO2, respectively.
Mn-containing or multiphase alloys form discontinuous mixed-oxide scales.
Al and Si have sufficiently high oxygen affinity to act as barrier-forming elements in these alloys.
A single-phase structure enables uniform diffusion and consequently controlled, slow-growing oxide formation.
Controlled, slow-growing oxide formation accommodates thermal stress and improves scale persistence.
Mn addition or a multiphase structure causes elemental segregation that disrupts uniform oxidation kinetics.
Disrupted oxidation kinetics cause rapid, uneven oxide growth and generate internal stresses.
Internal stresses generated by rapid, uneven oxide growth cause cracking and spallation.
Under identical exposure conditions, single-phase Al- or Si-containing alloys will have thinner, more uniform, and more adherent scales than Mn-containing or multiphase alloys.
Mn-containing or multiphase alloys will form thicker, more heterogeneous scales that crack or spall more readily.
The proposed behavior applies generally above 900 °C in controlled oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Changes in microstructural homogeneity or environmental conditions may alter the oxidation behavior.
